sources.h1: Crazy Tube Circuits Triptychon - Octave Fuzz / Drive / Treble Boost
sources.excerpt: Published on January 23, 2026 Crazy Tube Circuits fuzz octave fuzz overdrive treble boost pedal NAMM 2026 NAMM 2026 NAMM 2026 Information The Crazy Tube Circuits Triptychon is a fully analog multi-effect guitar pedal that combines a multi-voice fuzz circuit, a selectable upper octave or boost stage, and an assignable drive section within a single enclosure. The design follows a three-part concept intended to recreate the signal chain interaction found in classic recordings, where fuzz, octave effects, or treble boosters were driven into already overdriven amplifiers. Each section operates independently or in combination, allowing flexible routing and gain staging that reflects both vintage and modern pedalboard configurations. The central fuzz section forms the core of the circuit and features four selectable voices inspired by Dallas Arbiter Fuzz Face, Vox Tone Bender, Sola Sound Tone Bender Mk1.5, and Tone Bender MkII designs. It uses a custom configuration of metal-can silicon transistors engineered to replicate the dynamic response, cleanup behavior, and touch sensitivity associated with germanium-based fuzz circuits, while maintaining consistent performance across varying environmental conditions. The right-side section functions as either an upper octave fuzz or a boost circuit. In octave mode, it generates an upper octave effect with two selectable voicings, ranging from cleaner, more defined responses to louder and more harmonically rich textures inspired by classic octave fuzz designs. In boost mode, the circuit operates as a treble or mid-focused booster, with selectable voicings that shift between a traditional bright emphasis and a fuller midrange response. This section shares the same silicon transistor approach as the fuzz circuit to maintain consistent interaction characteristics. The left-side drive section is designed to replicate the response of a driven amplifier rather than functioning as a conventional standalone overdrive. It provides compression, sustain, and harmonic shaping that complements the fuzz and boost stages, allowing them to behave as they would when feeding an overdriven amp. The drive circuit can be assigned to operate in conjunction with either the fuzz or the octave or boost section, or controlled independently via an external footswitch connection. To address modern signal chain challenges, the pedal incorporates switchable anti-buffer circuits in both the fuzz and octave or boost sections. These circuits restore the impedance interaction typically lost when using buffered pedals, active pickups, or wireless systems, ensuring that the pedal responds correctly regardless of placement within a signal chain. Two onboard footswitches control combined activation of fuzz plus drive and octave or boost plus drive, while relay-based true bypass switching maintains signal integrity. Controls Drive Section Drive : Adjusts the gain level of the drive circuit Tone : Controls high-frequency response of the drive circuit Master : Sets the output level of the drive section Operation Assign Switch : Routes the drive section to the fuzz section, octave or boost section, or external control (XT) Fuzz Section Fuzz : Controls gain and intensity of the fuzz circuit Fuzz Voice Selector : Selects between four fuzz types (ff, vtb, 3/2, 2) Volume : Sets output level of the fuzz section (Anti) Buffer Pushbutton : Engages impedance-correcting circuit for use with buffered signals or active pickups Octave or Boost Section Gain : Controls output level of the octave or boost circuit Mode Toggle (OCT/BST) : Selects between upper octave fuzz and boost modes MOD Pushbutton : Boost mode: switches between treble boost and mid boost voicings Octave mode: switches between cleaner octave and more harmonically rich octave fuzz (Anti) Buffer Pushbutton : Engages impedance-correcting circuit for buffered signal chains Footswitches Left Footswitch : Activates fuzz section with assignable drive section Right Footswitch : Activates octave or boost section with assignable drive section Connections Input : 6.35 mm (1/4 inch) instrument input Output : 6.35 mm (1/4 inch) instrument output XT Connection : 6.35 mm (1/4 inch) jack for external footswitch control of the drive section Power Supply Input : External DC power connection Technical Specifications Power Supply : 9 V DC, center-negative Current Consumption : 80 mA Bypass Switching : Relay-based true bypass Circuit Type : Fully analog Transistors : Metal-can silicon transistors (fuzz and boost sections) Highlights Three-part architecture combining fuzz, octave or boost, and amp-style drive Four selectable fuzz voices based on Fuzz Face and Tone Bender circuits Silicon transistor design engineered for germanium-like response and stability Dual-mode section providing upper octave fuzz or treble or mid boost Drive circuit replicates the behavior of a driven amplifier Assignable routing of drive section with optional external control Switchable anti-buffer circuits for compatibility with modern pedalboards
